description: s441 round 4 (review round 3, finding 3). A handler that awaits a server call then uses the event a bound control method taken before the await (`event.preventDefault.bind(event)`). By then the browser has already acted on the event, so the control has no effect (the form submits). Rounds 2-3 matched call shapes and each shape was bypassed; round 4 POISONS the event binding after the first await: any use of the event, or of anything derived from it, other than a plain read of a non-control property is E-EVENT-CONTROL-AFTER-AWAIT. (s457 3a: the handler takes the event as the parameter of a `${(event) => { … }}` listener — a compiler-wrapped handler does not bind `event`, SPEC §5.2.)
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 10 (g-boot-event-cases-unhandled-server-call-s478)
rationale: §13.2: after a handler's first await, only plain reads of non-control event properties are allowed; every other use of the event or a value derived from it SHALL be E-EVENT-CONTROL-AFTER-AWAIT (§34). (S478 open-Qs ruling item 10: the server call is written as a handled statement — `const ok: bool = isOk(1) !{ _ :> false };` then `@verdict = ok ? … : …;` — since §19.9.10 makes an unhandled client call of a server function E-ERROR-002; the case's point is unchanged.)
